q.s: The excavation of Harappa, the first Indus site to be dug, was carried out in 1921 by:
q.x: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921; R. D. Banerji excavated Mohenjodaro (1922).

q.s: The Harappan port town of Lothal is situated on the banks of which river?
q.x: Lothal lies on the Bhogava near the Gulf of Khambhat; the Ravi is Harappa's river.

q.s: The National Maritime Heritage Complex being built at Lothal is located in which State?
q.x: Lothal is in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat; the complex is being built by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

q.s: Which Harappan site is famous for its tidal dockyard and is called the port city of the civilisation?
q.x: Lothal had a dockyard, warehouse and ship seals; Kalibangan is known for ploughed fields and fire altars.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, women and Shudras were denied which ceremony that marked initiation into Vedic study?
q.x: Upanayana (sacred-thread ceremony) was the initiation into Vedic study; its denial cut women off from the Vedas.

q.s: The Charvaka or Lokayata school of materialist philosophy is traditionally attributed to:
q.x: Charvaka materialism is credited to Brihaspati; Kapila founded Sankhya, Gautama Nyaya and Jaimini Mimamsa.

q.s: According to the Charvaka school, the only valid means of knowledge is:
q.x: The Charvakas accepted only perception and rejected inference and scriptural testimony.

q.s: Which of the four Vedas is chiefly associated with ceremonial chanting of hymns?
q.x: The Samaveda is a book of chants; the Yajurveda gives sacrificial formulae and the Atharvaveda spells and charms.

q.s: The Grihya Sutras of the Vedic literature deal mainly with:
q.x: Grihya Sutras prescribe household (domestic) ceremonies; Shrauta Sutras deal with the great public sacrifices.

q.s: The doctrine of transmigration of souls is first clearly found in which text?
q.x: Transmigration and moksha are first discussed in the Upanishads, starting with the Brihadaranyaka.

q.s: Mahapajapati Gotami, who brought up Siddhartha after his mother's death, was his:
q.x: Mahapajapati Gotami was his foster-mother and later the first Buddhist nun; Yashodhara was his wife.

q.s: Channa, associated with Siddhartha's Great Renunciation, was his:
q.x: Channa was the charioteer; Kanthaka was the horse.

q.s: Ashvaghosha, the author of the Buddhacharita, lived at the court of:
q.x: Ashvaghosha was a court poet of the Kushana king Kanishka.

q.s: Buddhaghosa, who composed the Visuddhimagga at Anuradhapura, was a scholar of which Buddhist school?
q.x: Buddhaghosa (5th century) was the great Theravada commentator in Sri Lanka.

q.s: The Buddhist university of Nalanda was sacked during the Turkish raids led by:
q.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed Nalanda c. 1193-1200 during his Bihar campaigns.

q.s: Which foreign writer was the first to mention the fortified towns and army of the Andhras?
q.x: Megasthenes' Indica credits the Andhras with 30 fortified towns and a large army.

q.s: Ashoka's Dhamma asked his subjects to show respect towards:
q.x: The edicts repeatedly ask for regard for both Brahmanas and Shramanas.

q.s: Ashoka's first Major Rock Edict prohibited:
q.x: Major Rock Edict I bans animal sacrifice and samajas (festive gatherings).

q.s: Ashoka appointed the Dhamma Mahamatras in which regnal year, as recorded in Rock Edict V?
q.x: Rock Edict V records the appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras in the 14th regnal year; the Kalinga war was in the 8th.

q.s: Ashoka's account of the Kalinga War and his remorse is found in:
q.x: Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war, about 1,50,000 deported and 1,00,000 killed.

q.s: The Kalinga War was fought in which regnal year of Ashoka?
q.x: The war came in Ashoka's 8th regnal year (c. 261 BCE), not the year of his coronation.

q.s: The rock-cut elephant at Dhauli in Odisha belongs to the age of the:
q.x: The Dhauli elephant (3rd century BCE) stands above Ashoka's rock edicts there.

q.s: The Ramagupta episode, in which Chandragupta II rescues queen Dhruvadevi from a Saka king, is narrated in:
q.x: Vishakhadatta's Devichandraguptam tells the story; Ramagupta ruled before Chandragupta II.

q.s: The later caves of Ajanta were patronised by which Vakataka ruler?
q.x: Harishena of the Vatsagulma branch patronised the later Ajanta caves.

q.s: The Kadamba dynasty of Banavasi was founded by:
q.x: Mayurasharma founded the Kadamba dynasty in the 4th century.

q.s: The Prakrit poem Setubandha was written by the Vakataka king:
q.x: Pravarasena II composed the Setubandha (Ravanavaho).

q.s: Jayadeva, the author of the Gita Govinda, was the court poet of:
q.x: Jayadeva adorned the court of the Sena king Lakshmana Sena, not the Palas.

q.s: Anantavarman Chodaganga, installed in Kalinga with Chola support, belonged to which dynasty?
q.x: Anantavarman Chodaganga was the great Eastern Ganga ruler who built the Jagannath temple at Puri.

q.s: The naval expedition of Rajendra Chola I in 1025 CE was directed against the kingdom of:
q.x: Rajendra I's 1025 expedition took Kadaram (Kedah) and places in Malaya and Sumatra from the Shailendras of Srivijaya.

q.s: Which Chola ruler completed the conquest of the whole of Sri Lanka, capturing its king Mahinda V?
q.x: Rajaraja I had conquered only northern Sri Lanka; Rajendra I took the whole island.

q.s: Who was the only Sultan of Delhi to die on the battlefield?
q.x: Ibrahim Lodi was killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat.

q.s: The First Battle of Panipat between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi was fought in:
q.x: Fought on 21 April 1526; 1556 was the Second Battle and 1761 the Third.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the Barid-i-Mumalik was the officer in charge of:
q.x: The Barid-i-Mumalik headed the state news and intelligence department; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was Chief Justice.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, criminal law was administered according to:
q.x: Criminal law followed the Sultan's own regulations (zawabit), while Hindus kept their personal laws.

q.s: Under the Mughals, the term jins-i-kamil ('perfect crops') referred to:
q.x: Jins-i-kamil were cash crops like cotton, sugarcane and indigo.

q.s: Which of the following crops was NOT introduced into India from the New World?
q.x: Indigo is native to India; tobacco, maize and chillies came from the Americas through the Portuguese.

q.s: Banda Bahadur was executed at Delhi in 1716 during the reign of the Mughal emperor:
q.x: Captured after the siege of Gurdas Nangal (1715), Banda was executed by Farrukhsiyar in 1716.

q.s: At which place did Banda Bahadur defeat Wazir Khan of Sirhind in 1710?
q.x: Banda defeated Wazir Khan at Chappar Chiri and took Sirhind in 1710.

q.s: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by:
q.x: Guru Arjan compiled it in 1604 and installed it in the Harmandir Sahib.

q.s: The final version of the Guru Granth Sahib was prepared by Guru Gobind Singh in 1705 at:
q.x: It was finalised at Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo), adding the hymns of Guru Tegh Bahadur.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Bhakti movement is correct?
o: It insisted on Sanskrit as the only language of devotion.
It made the jnana marga the main path for ordinary people.
It strengthened caste barriers in worship.
It arose partly as a reaction against ritualism, priestly dominance and caste.
q.x: Bhakti reacted against ritual, priests and caste, and offered devotion because the jnana and karma margas were too hard for common people.

q.s: Which of the following Maratha forts is a Jal Durg (sea fort)?
q.x: Sindhudurg and Khanderi are sea forts on the Konkan coast; Raigad, Torna and Vishalgad are hill forts.

q.s: The 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India' were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: The twelve forts were inscribed in July 2025.

q.s: The Treaty of Bassein (1802), which led to the Second Anglo-Maratha War, was signed by the British with:
q.x: After Holkar's victory at Poona, Baji Rao II fled to the British and accepted a subsidiary alliance at Bassein.

q.s: The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) divided newly discovered lands outside Europe between:
q.x: The line was drawn 370 leagues west of Cape Verde; lands east went to Portugal and west to Spain.

q.s: From whom did Francois Martin obtain Pondicherry for the French in 1674?
q.x: Pondicherry was granted by Sher Khan Lodi; Karaikal was bought from the Raja of Tanjore in 1739.

q.s: The Portuguese were allowed to settle at Hooghly in Bengal by a farman of:
q.x: Akbar's farman allowed the Portuguese at Hooghly; Shah Jahan expelled them in 1632.

q.s: Which ruler allowed the Portuguese to build a fort at Diu in 1535?
q.x: Pressed by Humayun, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat allowed the Diu fort in 1535.

q.s: Which former French settlement in the Andhra region remained under French control until 1954?
q.x: Yanam, founded by the French in 1723, was their only territory in Andhra and merged with India in 1954.

q.s: Tranquebar on the Coromandel coast was a settlement of the:
q.x: Tranquebar (1620) and Serampore were Danish; their legacy was mainly missionary and educational.

q.s: The book 'India Wins Freedom' was written by:
q.x: Azad wrote India Wins Freedom; Rajendra Prasad wrote India Divided and Bose The Indian Struggle.

q.s: The practice of Sati was abolished in 1829 during the tenure of:
q.x: Bentinck's Regulation XVII of 1829 abolished Sati, which later fed fears of interference in religion.

q.s: Annapurnayya, known as 'Andhra Netaji', was imprisoned for his article 'Chicharapidugu' on:
q.x: He received 18 months' rigorous imprisonment for writing on the 1857 revolt.

q.s: The Third Carnatic War was the Indian theatre of which European war?
q.x: The Third Carnatic War (1756-63) coincided with the Seven Years' War and ended with the Treaty of Paris (1763).

q.s: In the Battle of Wandiwash (1760), the French forces were led by:
q.x: Sir Eyre Coote defeated Lally at Wandiwash; Lally had weakened the Deccan by recalling Bussy.

q.s: The Talpur Amirs of Sindh were defeated at Miani and Dabo in 1843 by:
q.x: Napier's victories led to the annexation of Sindh under Ellenborough.

q.s: Which of the following states was NOT annexed under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse?
q.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on grounds of misgovernment; Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur lapsed.

q.s: Under Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance, the cost of the British army stationed in an Indian state was borne by:
q.x: The state paid a subsidy or ceded territory to maintain the subsidiary force.

q.s: Which was the first Indian state to accept Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance, in 1798?
q.x: The Nizam of Hyderabad signed first (1798) and later ceded the 'Ceded Districts' (1800).

q.s: Slavery was abolished in British India by Act V of 1843 during the tenure of:
q.x: Ellenborough, who also ended the First Afghan War, passed Act V of 1843.

q.s: The Hunter Commission on education (1882) was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Hunter - Ripon; Raleigh - Curzon; Hartog - Irwin.

q.s: The Hartog Committee (1929) on education was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The Hartog Committee was an auxiliary of the Simon Commission under Irwin.

q.s: The Indian Universities Act, 1904 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: Curzon's Raleigh Commission (1902) led to the 1904 Act, which increased government control over universities.

q.s: Who is called the 'Father of the Communal Electorate' in India?
q.x: Lord Minto, viceroy at the time of the 1909 reforms, is so called.

q.s: The Indian National Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims under the:
q.x: At Lucknow (1916) the Congress and the League agreed on separate electorates.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 is correct?
o: Morley intended them to lead to a parliamentary system.
They introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
They introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
They made the executive responsible to the legislature.
q.x: The 1909 Act brought separate electorates; councils stayed advisory and dyarchy came in 1919.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: The 1935 Act enfranchised only about 14 per cent of the population.

q.s: 'States and Minorities', which proposed State ownership of agricultural land and collective farming, was written by:
q.x: Ambedkar's memorandum (1947) proposed State socialism written into the Constitution.

q.s: Who described the Indian village as 'a sink of localism' in the Constituent Assembly?
q.x: Ambedkar said this on 4 November 1948, preferring the individual as the unit of the polity.

q.s: The Akali movement for the reform of gurdwaras grew out of the:
q.x: The Singh Sabha promoted Gurmukhi and removed un-Sikh practices; the Akali movement followed from it.

q.s: The Vernacular Press Act (1878), which gagged the Indian-language press, was passed under:
q.x: Lytton's Vernacular Press Act was repealed by Ripon in 1882.

q.s: The Servants of India Society was founded at Poona in 1905 by:
q.x: Gokhale founded it on 12 June 1905 to train national workers by constitutional means; Ranade was his guru.

q.s: 'Nil Darpan', the play on the oppression of indigo cultivators in Bengal, was written by:
q.x: Dinabandhu Mitra wrote it; Michael Madhusudan Dutt translated it into English and Rev. James Long published it.

q.s: The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 was led by Digambar and Bishnu Biswas of which district of Bengal?
q.x: The Biswas brothers of Nadia led the revolt; Pabna is linked with the agrarian league of 1873.

q.s: Who translated Gandhi's speech at Vijayawada in April 1919 during the Rowlatt Satyagraha?
q.x: Kaleswara Rao translated the 8 April 1919 speech; Konda Venkatappayya led the Guntur Bar's demand to jail Dyer.

q.s: The first sitting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946 was presided over by its temporary President:
q.x: Sachchidananda Sinha presided as the senior-most member; Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December.

q.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be:
q.x: 389 = 296 from British India + 93 from the princely states; after Partition it became 299.

q.s: Gandhi's concept of 'Trusteeship' means that:
o: The rich should hold their wealth in trust for the welfare of society
All industries should be owned by the State
Wealth should be distributed equally by law
Private property should be abolished by force
q.x: Trusteeship asks the wealthy to treat surplus wealth as held in trust for society; Gandhi linked it to his South African years.

q.s: Who gave the title 'Rani' to the Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu?
q.x: Nehru called her 'Rani' after meeting her in Shillong jail in 1937.

q.s: Who was the first to hoist the Indian national flag abroad, at Stuttgart in 1907?
q.x: Madame Cama unfurled the flag at the International Socialist Congress, Stuttgart.

q.s: The first woman to become Governor of an Indian State was:
q.x: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of the United Provinces in 1947; Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister.

q.s: India's first university of health sciences, set up in Andhra Pradesh in 1986, is the:
q.x: The NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada (1986), was the first health university in India.

q.s: Vinoba Bhave launched the Bhoodan Movement on 18 April 1951 at:
q.x: It began at Pochampalli (Nalgonda); Mangroth in UP became the first Gramdan village in 1952.

q.s: Who was the first land donor of the Bhoodan Movement, giving 100 acres at Pochampalli?
q.x: Vedire Ramachandra Reddy donated the first 100 acres.

q.s: The first session of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha (Madras, 1934) demanded the establishment of a university at:
q.x: The 1934 session under Nemali Pattabhirama Rao asked for a university at Tirupati; S. V. University came in 1954.

q.s: The Special Andhra Sabha at Madras in 1931, under Kadapa Koti Reddy, handed its resolution to Gandhi for presentation at the:
q.x: Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference (1931).

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission set up in 1953 was headed by:
q.x: Fazl Ali chaired it; Panikkar and Kunzru were members; S. K. Dhar headed the 1948 Linguistic Provinces Commission.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the States Reorganisation Commission is correct?
o: It treated language as an important factor but not the only one.
It recommended keeping the Part A, B and C classification of states.
It accepted 'one language, one state' as its guiding rule.
It ignored administrative efficiency and financial viability.
q.x: The SRC rejected 'one language, one state' and gave weight to unity, security, administrative and financial viability.

q.s: Which of the following leaders of Hyderabad State opposed the formation of Visalandhra?
q.x: Chenna Reddy opposed Visalandhra throughout; Burgula, Narendraji and Mandumula Narsing Rao supported it.

q.s: The Sakas who settled in India were absorbed into Indian society as:
q.x: Foreign ruling groups like the Sakas were given the status of 'fallen' (vratya) Kshatriyas.

q.s: The Saka era, used by the Western Kshatrapas on their records and coins, began in:
q.x: The Saka era began in 78 CE; 57 BCE is the Vikrama era and 320 CE the Gupta era.

q.s: Gunadhya's Brihatkatha, composed in the Satavahana period, was written in which language?
q.x: The Paishachi original is lost; it survives through later Sanskrit versions.

q.s: Which later Sanskrit work preserves the stories of Gunadhya's Brihatkatha?
q.x: Somadeva's Kathasaritsagara (11th century) retells the Brihatkatha; the Gathasaptasati is Hala's Prakrit anthology.

q.s: Under the Satavahanas, the Nigama Sabha mentioned in the Bhattiprolu inscription was:
q.x: The Nigama Sabha ran towns; villages were headed by the Gramika and a gulma was a military outpost.

q.s: In the early phase of Amaravati art, the Buddha was represented through:
o: Symbols such as the throne, footprints and stupa
q.x: The early Amaravati ayakapatas show the Buddha only through symbols, in the Hinayana tradition.

q.s: Under the Vishnukundins, the term 'Vishti' referred to:
q.x: Vishti (vetti in Telugu) was forced labour; Bhaga was the one-sixth share of produce and the Gulmika a border officer.

q.s: Which Eastern Chalukya (Vengi) king was the only one to embrace Jainism?
q.x: Vimaladitya became a Jain; Potlacheruvu was a noted Jain centre in the period.

q.s: To restore Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne, Tikkana went as envoy to the Kakatiya ruler:
q.x: Ganapatideva sent forces at Tikkana's request and reinstated Manumasiddhi II.

q.s: Jayapa Senani, head of the elephant corps of Kakatiya Ganapatideva, wrote which treatise on dance?
q.x: Jayapa (Gaja Sahini) wrote Nritta Ratnavali; Sangita Ratnakara is by Sarngadeva.

q.s: According to tradition, Prataparudra II divided the Kakatiya kingdom into how many Nayankaras?
q.x: There were 77 Nayankaras held by Nayakas, who kept troops and paid a fixed tribute.

q.s: The Kakatiya Nayankara system continued under Vijayanagara in the form of the:
q.x: It evolved into the Vijayanagara Amaranayakas and later the Poligars.

q.s: The Motupalli inscription, the chief commercial document of the Kakatiya period, was issued by:
q.x: Ganapatideva's abhaya sasana at Motupalli assured protection and fair duties to foreign merchants.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Kakatiya period is correct?
o: Jainism was declared the state religion.
Veerashaivism was suppressed by the rulers.
Non-Brahmanisation of religion and politics reached its culmination.
Officials were drawn only from Brahmin families.
q.x: Non-Brahmanical trends peaked; officials came also from warrior and peasant groups, and Veerashaiva sects flourished.

q.s: Coins of Harihara I and Bukka I of Vijayanagara bore the figure of:
q.x: Hanuman appears on the early Sangama coins; Venkateswara and Balakrishna on Krishnadevaraya's and Garuda on Achyutaraya's.

q.s: Art critics hold that the gopurams surpassing those of the Vittala temple at Hampi are found at:
q.x: The gopurams of the Tadipatri temples are counted the finest; Lepakshi is famed for its paintings.

q.s: In the Battle of Bobbili (1757), Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram was supported by the French under:
q.x: Bussy, who held the Northern Circars after the Treaty of Aurangabad (1753), joined Vijayarama Raju against Ranga Rao.

q.s: Who killed Vijayarama Raju in his camp after the fall of Bobbili fort?
q.x: Tandra Paparayudu avenged the fall of Bobbili by killing Vijayarama Raju.

q.s: The Wahabi conspiracy of 1839 in Hyderabad State was led by:
q.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula, the Nizam's brother, was imprisoned in Golconda Fort; Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin led the 1857 attack on the Residency.

q.s: The Telugu nationalist journal 'Krishna Patrika' is associated with:
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited the Krishna Patrika; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded the Andhra Patrika.

q.s: Gurajada Apparao's famous play 'Kanyasulkam' deals with the social evil of:
q.x: Kanyasulkam (1892) satirises the sale of young girls in marriage (bride-price).

q.s: Gurajada Apparao championed the use of which idiom in Telugu literature?
q.x: He was a pioneer of the spoken idiom along with Gidugu Ramamurthy.

q.s: Who is known as the 'Granthalaya Pitamaha' (father of the library movement) of Andhra?
q.x: Ayyanki is Granthalaya Pitamaha; Velaga Venkatappayya is called 'Library Gandhi'.

q.s: Ambedkar moved the Draft Constitution for consideration in the Constituent Assembly on:
q.x: He moved it on 4 November 1948; the Drafting Committee was formed on 29 August 1947 and the Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the share of urban population in India was about:
q.x: Urban share was 31.16% in 2011 (27.8% in 2001); 68.8% was rural.

q.s: According to Census 2001, the largest urban agglomeration of India was:
q.x: In 2001 the order was Greater Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi.

q.s: The NAMASTE scheme launched in 2023 is meant for:
o: Safety and dignity of sanitation workers
q.x: NAMASTE, run by the Social Justice and Housing & Urban Affairs ministries, aims at zero sanitation-work fatalities.

q.s: The Liberhan Commission was appointed to inquire into:
o: The demolition at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992
q.x: Liberhan - Ayodhya; Srikrishna - Bombay riots; Wadhwa - Graham Staines; Jain - Rajiv Gandhi conspiracy.

q.s: The Srikrishna Commission inquired into:
q.x: Justice B. N. Srikrishna probed the Bombay riots that followed the Ayodhya demolition.

q.s: 'Direct Action Day', which set off large-scale communal riots in Calcutta, was called by the Muslim League on:
q.x: The riots after Direct Action Day pushed the Congress to accept Partition; 23 March 1940 is the Lahore Resolution.

q.s: In which 2018 case did the Supreme Court hold that khap panchayat interference in the marriage of consenting adults is illegal?
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
Shakti Vahini v. Union of India
Lata Singh v. State of U.P.
q.x: Shakti Vahini (2018) laid down measures against honour crimes; Lata Singh (2006) also protected inter-caste marriage but predates it.

q.s: The concept of 'street-level bureaucracy' in public policy was given by:
q.x: Lipsky (1980) studied front-line officials; Pressman and Wildavsky wrote the top-down study 'Implementation' (1973).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a targeted social welfare service?
o: General health services for all citizens
q.x: Social welfare services are targeted at vulnerable groups; a general service for everyone is not.

q.s: The Akshaya Patra Foundation, which runs India's largest NGO mid-day meal programme, is based in:
q.x: Akshaya Patra was founded in Bengaluru in 2000.

q.s: Mission Vatsalya for child protection subsumed which earlier scheme?
q.x: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the ICPS; ICDS continues under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.

q.s: Under Mission Vatsalya, sponsorship and foster-care support per child per month is:
q.x: Support is Rs 4,000 per child per month; aftercare covers 18-21 years.

q.s: The SMILE scheme for transgender persons and persons engaged in begging is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: SMILE (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise) is run by MoSJE; Garima Greh are shelter homes under it.

q.s: The wage ceiling for coverage under the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) scheme is:
q.x: ESIC covers employees earning up to Rs 21,000 a month (Rs 25,000 for persons with disability).

q.s: The four Labour Codes together replaced how many central labour laws?
q.x: The Codes on Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security and OSH subsume 29 central laws.

q.s: All four Labour Codes were brought into force on:
q.x: All four Codes came into force together on 21 November 2025.

q.s: The Atal Pension Yojana is administered by the:
o: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
q.x: APY (2015) is run by PFRDA and replaced the Swavalamban scheme; it guarantees Rs 1,000-5,000 a month from 60.

q.s: The guaranteed monthly pension under the Atal Pension Yojana ranges from:
q.x: APY guarantees Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month from age 60, depending on contribution.

q.s: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on:
q.x: SBM was launched on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2014.

q.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, the first law enforcing Article 17, was originally enacted as the:
o: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
q.x: It was renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act in 1976.

q.s: The office of the Special Officer (Commissioner) for Linguistic Minorities is provided under:
q.x: Article 350B (inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956) provides for it; 350A deals with mother-tongue instruction at primary stage.

q.s: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the:
q.x: The CLM office is under the Ministry of Minority Affairs; linguistic minorities are identified State-wise.

q.s: The Kartarpur Corridor links Dera Baba Nanak in Gurdaspur with which gurdwara in Pakistan?
q.x: The 4.7-km visa-free corridor runs to Darbar Sahib in Narowal district, where Guru Nanak spent his last years.

q.s: The Kartarpur Corridor was inaugurated in November 2019 to mark:
o: The 400th birth anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur
The 350th birth anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh
The 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak
q.x: It opened on 9 November 2019 for Guru Nanak's 550th Prakash Purab.

q.s: The Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh boundary dispute between India and Nepal is rooted in which treaty?
q.x: The Sugauli Treaty made the Kali (Mahakali) river the boundary; its source is disputed and Nepal issued a new map in 2020.

q.s: The Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project is a part of which India-Nepal agreement?
q.x: The Mahakali Treaty (1996) covers Sarada, Tanakpur and Pancheshwar; Kosi was 1954 and Gandak 1959.

q.s: The Kudankulam nuclear power plant, built with Russian cooperation, is located in:
q.x: Kudankulam is in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The name of the BrahMos missile is derived from:
q.x: BrahMos, an India-Russia joint venture, is named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.

q.s: The annual Emissions Gap Report is published by:
q.x: UNEP publishes the Emissions Gap Report; the 2025 edition put current policies on course for about 2.8 C.

q.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, members of the legislative councils could:
o: Discuss the budget but not vote on it
q.x: The 1892 Act allowed budget discussion and questions with notice, but no voting and no supplementaries.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment replaced the words 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352?
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) made this change after the 1975 Emergency.

q.s: The term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies was raised from five to six years by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) raised it to six years; the 44th restored five.

q.s: The right to privacy was declared a Fundamental Right by a nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court in:
o: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
M. P. Sharma v. Satish Chandra
K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Kharak Singh v. State of U.P.
q.x: Puttaswamy unanimously recognised privacy under Article 21, overruling M. P. Sharma and Kharak Singh on this point.

q.s: The right to property is at present a constitutional (legal) right under Article:
q.x: Article 300A was inserted by the 44th Amendment; it is enforced under Article 226 or by suit, not Article 32.

q.s: The right to property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A.

q.s: Before 1950, the power to issue writs was available only to the High Courts of:
q.x: Only the three Presidency High Courts could issue writs before the Constitution.

q.s: Which writ can be issued against private individuals as well as public authorities?
q.x: Habeas Corpus lies against anyone detaining a person; Certiorari and Prohibition lie only against judicial or quasi-judicial bodies.

q.s: In Kihoto Hollohan (1992), the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the:
q.x: It upheld the Tenth Schedule added by the 52nd Amendment but made the Speaker's decision open to judicial review.

q.s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Caste cannot be a criterion of backwardness
Reservation can exceed 50 per cent as a rule
There shall be no reservation in promotions
The creamy layer must be included in OBC quota
q.x: Indra Sawhney upheld OBC reservation with a creamy-layer exclusion, a 50% ceiling and no reservation in promotions.

q.s: The First Backward Classes Commission, set up in 1953, was headed by:
q.x: Kaka Kalelkar headed the first commission; B. P. Mandal headed the second (1979).

q.s: The Second Backward Classes Commission headed by B. P. Mandal was set up by the government of:
q.x: The Janata Government of Morarji Desai set it up in 1979; V. P. Singh implemented it in 1990.

q.s: Which clause of Article 39 directs that the ownership and control of material resources be distributed to subserve the common good?
q.x: 39(b) - material resources; 39(c) - no concentration of wealth; 39(e) - health of workers and children; 39(f) - children's development.

q.s: Article 1 of the Constitution describes India as:
q.x: Ambedkar explained 'Union' was used because it is not the result of an agreement among States and no State can secede.

q.s: The members of the Rajya Sabha from the National Capital Territory of Delhi are elected by:
o: The Lok Sabha members from Delhi
The councillors of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi
The elected members of the Delhi Legislative Assembly
q.x: Delhi's three Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected MLAs of the Delhi Assembly.

q.s: Which of the following Union Territories does NOT elect members to the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: Only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir, which have legislatures, elect Rajya Sabha members.

q.s: In Sita Soren v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court overruled which judgment on legislators' immunity for taking bribes?
q.x: Sita Soren held that bribery is not protected by parliamentary privilege.

q.s: A member of Parliament is free from arrest in civil cases during a session and for how many days before and after it?
q.x: The freedom from civil arrest covers the session and 40 days before and after.

q.s: The Articles dealing with Parliament (Articles 79 to 122) are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
q.x: Part V covers the Union; Part VI covers the States.

q.s: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha to face a motion for removal, in 1954?
q.x: Mavalankar faced the first removal motion (1954); Hukam Singh (1966) and Balram Jakhar (1987) faced later ones.

q.s: The Government Chief Whip in the Lok Sabha is the:
o: Leader of the House in the Rajya Sabha
q.x: The office of Whip rests on convention; the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs acts as the Government Chief Whip.

q.s: A 'three-line whip' issued by a party to its members:
o: Merely informs them of a vote
Directs them to vote strictly as the party directs
q.x: A one-line whip only informs; a three-line whip is a strict direction to vote with the party.

q.s: The Committee on Petitions of the Rajya Sabha consists of how many members?
q.x: The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions has 10 members; the Lok Sabha one has 15.

q.s: Under Article 85, the maximum gap allowed between two sessions of Parliament is:
q.x: Not more than six months may pass between the last sitting of one session and the first of the next; Article 174 does the same for States.

q.s: How many times have joint sittings of the two Houses of Parliament been held so far?
q.x: Joint sittings: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978) and POTA (2002).

q.s: During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend the term of a State Legislative Assembly by law for:
q.x: Extension is one year at a time and cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency ends.

q.s: Which Article makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman; Article 63 creates the office.

q.s: Cabinet Committees of the Union Government are set up under the:
o: Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961
q.x: Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional bodies formed by the PM under the Transaction of Business Rules; GoMs and EGoMs were abolished in 2014.

q.s: The Attorney General of India holds office:
o: For a fixed term of five years
During the pleasure of the President
q.x: The Constitution fixes no term; he resigns with the government only by convention, and his remuneration is fixed by the President.

q.s: In Subhash Desai (2023), the Supreme Court held that the whip of a party in the legislature is appointed by:
q.x: The political party, not the legislature party, appoints the whip and the leader.

q.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the:
q.x: Section 22 of the NGT Act provides appeal directly to the Supreme Court.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
q.x: The NGT sits at New Delhi (Principal Bench) with zonal benches at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai.

q.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment?
q.x: The five transferred were education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice; police and public order remain State subjects.

q.s: 'Protection of wild animals and birds' is a subject in the:
q.x: It is Entry 17B of the Concurrent List, inserted by the 42nd Amendment; Entry 17 is prevention of cruelty to animals.

q.s: 'Adulteration of foodstuffs and other goods' falls under which list of the Seventh Schedule?
q.x: It is in the Concurrent List; forests moved from the State to the Concurrent List in 1976.

q.s: Residuary powers of legislation in India are vested in Parliament by:
q.x: Article 248 with Entry 97 of the Union List vests residuary powers in Parliament.

q.s: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article:
q.x: Article 280 (Part XII) provides for it every fifth year or earlier; Article 275 is about grants-in-aid.

q.s: The First Finance Commission, constituted in 1951, was chaired by:
q.x: K. C. Neogy chaired the first FC.

q.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission was chaired by:
q.x: N. K. Singh chaired the 15th; Y. V. Reddy the 14th and Vijay Kelkar the 13th.

q.s: Under the Constitution, which of the following is barred from holding any further office under the Government after ceasing to hold office?
q.x: Article 148(4) bars the CAG; the Constitution does not similarly bar Election Commissioners.

q.s: A performance audit conducted by the CAG mainly examines:
q.x: Performance audit tests the 3 Es; financial attest audit checks whether accounts are true.

q.s: NITI Aayog, set up on 1 January 2015, is a/an:
o: Executive body created by a Cabinet resolution
q.x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission by a Cabinet resolution; it is neither statutory nor constitutional.

q.s: Which of the following is a quasi-judicial body?
q.x: Quasi-judicial bodies like the CIC, NHRC and SEBI can apply law, summon and sanction but are not courts.

q.s: Which of the following bodies has the powers of a civil court while inquiring into complaints?
q.x: The NCST (and NCSC, NCBC) has civil-court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records.

q.s: The Vienna Declaration (1993) affirmed that human rights are:
o: Only civil and political in nature
q.x: The Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action stressed the indivisibility of human rights.

q.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, about 73 per cent of prison inmates in India were:
q.x: Undertrials, not convicts, made up about 73% of inmates.

q.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, the highest prison occupancy rate was recorded in:
q.x: Delhi had the highest occupancy (194.6%), followed by Meghalaya; the national rate was 112.7%.

q.s: The committee that recommends the appointment of a State Chief Information Commissioner is chaired by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: The committee is the CM, the Leader of the Opposition and a Cabinet Minister; the Governor appoints.

q.s: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is headquartered in:
q.x: UNODC is in Vienna; UNCAC was adopted at Merida (2003) and UNTOC at Palermo (2000).

q.s: India ratified the UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) in:
q.x: India signed UNCAC in 2005 and ratified it in 2011.

q.s: The 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes to:
q.x: The 14th FC raised it from 32% to 42% and drew no distinction between special and general category States.

q.s: The Commission on Centre-State Relations set up in 1983 was headed by:
q.x: Sarkaria (1983); Punchhi (2007); Rajamannar (Tamil Nadu, 1969).

q.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2005) was first chaired by:
q.x: Moily chaired the second ARC; the first ARC (1966) was under Morarji Desai, then K. Hanumanthaiah.

q.s: The orders of which body have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court?
q.x: Delimitation Commission orders cannot be challenged in court or modified by legislatures.

q.s: The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill (1989) on Panchayati Raj:
o: Was passed and became the 64th Amendment
Was defeated in the Lok Sabha
Passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha
q.x: It failed in the Rajya Sabha; the 73rd Amendment (1992) later gave shape to Article 40.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organise village panchayats?
q.x: Article 40 is a Directive Principle in Part IV.

q.s: The Community Development Programme was launched in India in:
q.x: CDP began on 2 October 1952; the National Extension Service followed in 1953.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission, constituted on 31 December 2023, is chaired by:
q.x: Dr Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC (award period 2026-31).

q.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission reduced the States' share from 42% to 41% mainly because:
o: Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory
Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh
q.x: The 1% cut accounted for the new UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

q.s: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed every year on:
q.x: 24 April marks the coming into force of the 73rd Amendment in 1993.

q.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, defeated in the Lok Sabha in April 2026, sought to raise the strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to:
q.x: The Bill (550 to 850 seats) got 298-230 votes, short of the 352 needed under Article 368.

q.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was created as a separate body under Article 338A by the:
q.x: The 89th Amendment split the old commission; the NCST began functioning on 19 February 2004. The 102nd gave NCBC constitutional status.

q.s: The Fifth Schedule dealing with Scheduled Areas is provided under Article:
q.x: 244(1) - Fifth Schedule; 244(2) - Sixth Schedule (tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram).

q.s: The strategy of NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme rests on:
q.x: The ADP works through convergence of schemes, collaboration and competition among districts via monthly delta rankings.

q.s: Under the Aspirational Districts Programme, which two themes carry the highest weight of 30 per cent each?
q.x: Health & Nutrition and Education carry 30% each; Agriculture & Water 20%; Financial Inclusion & Skills and Basic Infrastructure 10% each.

q.s: The PMGDISHA scheme of the Government of India aims at:
o: Promotion of digital payments by merchants
Laying optical fibre to gram panchayats
q.x: PMGDISHA tackles the skills side of the digital divide; BharatNet covers infrastructure and PM-WANI public Wi-Fi.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of e-governance?
q.x: E-governance creates and strengthens audit trails, so their removal cannot be a benefit.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the State with the highest proportion of Scheduled Caste population is:
q.x: Punjab has the highest SC share (about 32%); Uttar Pradesh has the largest SC population in absolute numbers.

q.s: As per Census 2011, which State has the largest Scheduled Tribe population?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population; Mizoram has the highest ST share.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the largest tribe of India is the:
q.x: The Bhils are the largest tribe, followed by the Gonds; STs formed 8.6% of the population.

q.s: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, the minimum service level of tap water supply for rural households is:
q.x: JJM assures 55 lpcd of prescribed quality; a 'Har Ghar Jal' village is certified by a Gram Sabha resolution.

q.s: PMAY-Urban 2.0, launched in 2024, aims at building how many more urban houses?
q.x: PMAY-U 2.0 targets 1 crore houses; In-situ Slum Redevelopment was dropped as a vertical.

q.s: Gross National Product (GNP) is equal to:
o: GDP plus net factor income from abroad
q.x: GNP = GDP + NFIA; India's NFIA is usually negative, so its GNP is below GDP.

q.s: In India, estimates of saving and capital formation by institutional sector are released by the:
q.x: The NSO of MoSPI publishes the National Accounts Statistics; NAS 2025 showed household saving at 18.1% of GDP in 2023-24.

q.s: The India Employment Report 2024 was released by the ILO together with the:
q.x: The ILO and the Institute for Human Development jointly released the India Employment Report 2024.

q.s: Under which approach of measuring employment is a person counted as employed if he worked at least one hour on any day of the preceding seven days?
q.x: CWS uses a 7-day reference with one hour on any day; UPS uses 365 days; CDS counts each day in half-day units.

q.s: The Modified Mixed Reference Period (MMRP) was first used for poverty estimation in India by the:
q.x: Tendulkar used MRP consumption; Rangarajan (2014) first used MMRP, which raised measured consumption.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Indira Kranthi Patham (2004-05) was formed by merging the Velugu project with:
q.x: IKP merged Velugu (World Bank-aided) and DWCRA, under SERP.

q.s: MEPMA, set up in Andhra Pradesh in 2007, deals with:
o: Self-help groups of the urban poor
q.x: MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas) organises urban SHGs; SERP works with the rural poor.

q.s: About one-third of the outlay of the First Five Year Plan (1951-56) went to:
q.x: The First Plan gave top priority to agriculture and irrigation (Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud); heavy industry got priority in the Second Plan.

q.s: Under the Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (1992), what share of export earnings could be converted at the market rate?
q.x: LERMS (March 1992) allowed 60% at the market rate and 40% at the official rate; full float came in 1993.

q.s: SEBI was given statutory status under the SEBI Act in:
q.x: SEBI was set up in 1988 as a non-statutory body and made statutory by the SEBI Act, 1992.

q.s: The one-time 'Urbanisation Premium' grant recommended by the 16th Finance Commission is linked to:
o: Merging peri-urban villages into urban local bodies
q.x: The Rs 10,000 crore premium rewards States that adopt a Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy for peri-urban villages.

q.s: Which Andhra Pradesh district held the 1st rank in the baseline ranking of the Aspirational Districts Programme in March 2018?
q.x: Vizianagaram led the baseline ranking but slipped to 4th in the first delta ranking (May 2018).

q.s: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised on:
q.x: It was nationalised under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948; 19 July 1969 was bank nationalisation.

q.s: Since 2020-21, the accounting year of the Reserve Bank of India runs from:
q.x: The RBI moved from a July-June year to April-March from 2020-21.

q.s: Under the RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility, the floor of the policy rate corridor is formed by the:
q.x: The SDF is the floor; the MSF and bank rate form the ceiling, with the repo rate in between.

q.s: The PRASHAD scheme of the Ministry of Tourism relates to:
q.x: PRASHAD - pilgrimage; Swadesh Darshan - thematic circuits; NIDHI - hospitality database.

q.s: According to the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how many District Cooperative Central Banks (DCCBs) are there in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: AP has 13 DCCBs and 2,024 PACS.

q.s: The Malegam Committee appointed by the RBI after the Andhra Pradesh crisis of 2010 dealt with:
q.x: It recommended caps such as not more than two MFIs lending to a borrower.

q.s: The Banking Ombudsman in India is appointed by the:
q.x: Under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, the RBI appoints the Ombudsman; the scheme began in 1995.

q.s: Under the RBI's April 2024 norms, a small finance bank seeking to become a universal bank must have a minimum net worth of:
q.x: It needs Rs 1,000 crore net worth and a 5-year satisfactory record; AU SFB got approval in 2025.

q.s: The 'twin balance sheet problem' in the Indian economy refers to stressed balance sheets of:
q.x: Over-leveraged companies and NPA-laden banks together slowed credit and investment (Economic Survey 2016-17).

q.s: The Harshad Mehta scam of 1992 involved the misuse of:
o: Cooperative bank deposits for real estate
Ready-forward deals in government securities and fake bank receipts
q.x: Bank funds were diverted into stocks via ready-forward G-Sec deals and fake bank receipts.

q.s: The reconstruction of Yes Bank in 2020 was led by:
q.x: After an RBI moratorium, an SBI-led consortium recapitalised Yes Bank.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is correct?
o: It covers goods only and not services.
It covers both goods and services.
It is compiled by the National Statistics Office.
Primary articles have the largest weight in the 2011-12 series.
q.x: WPI covers goods only; manufactured products have the largest weight; it is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.

q.s: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI was signed in:
q.x: The MPFA was signed in February 2015; the RBI Act was amended in 2016 to give flexible inflation targeting a statutory basis.

q.s: According to Musgrave, the provision of public goods such as the judiciary and defence comes under the budget's:
q.x: Allocation provides public goods; distribution deals with equity; stabilisation controls inflation and unemployment.

q.s: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced in India by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
q.x: The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced GST; the 115th Amendment Bill of 2011 lapsed.

q.s: GST in India was first proposed during the government of:
q.x: The Vajpayee government set up the Empowered Committee in 2000, first chaired by Asim Dasgupta.

q.s: Large net foreign investment inflows into India generally cause the rupee to:
q.x: Inflows raise the supply of dollars, so the rupee tends to appreciate even when imports rise.

q.s: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 led to the creation of:
q.x: 44 nations met in New Hampshire; India was a founding member of the IMF (27 December 1945).

q.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Prakasam Committee (1938) recommended abolition of zamindari estates in Madras Presidency.

q.s: 'Operation Barga' for recording sharecroppers was carried out in:
q.x: The Left Front government in West Bengal recorded bargadars, giving them heritable rights.

q.s: Under the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS), claims are paid when:
o: Observed weather deviates from specified trigger levels
Yield falls due to poor-quality seed
The farmer fails to sow on time
q.x: RWBCIS uses weather parameters as proxies for crop loss.

q.s: The Shanta Kumar High Level Committee (2015) dealt with the restructuring of:
q.x: It recommended handing procurement in surplus States to the States so FCI could focus on the east.

q.s: The Shanta Kumar Committee recommended that NFSA coverage be reduced from 67 per cent to:
q.x: It proposed cutting coverage to 40% and estimated PDS leakage at 46%.

q.s: The main imported raw material of India's steel industry is:
q.x: India has ample iron ore but imports most of its coking coal.

q.s: In 2024, India's rank among the world's crude steel producers was:
q.x: India was second to China with about 149 million tonnes.

q.s: District Industries Centres (DICs) were introduced under the Industrial Policy of:
q.x: The 1977 policy of the Janata Government set up DICs to promote small and cottage industries.

q.s: The policy of reserving items for exclusive manufacture in the small-scale sector began in:
q.x: Reservation began in 1967, peaked at about 873 items in 1984, and the last 20 items were dereserved in 2015.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (old law - law that replaced it) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: FERA was replaced by FEMA, 1999; the PMLA is an anti-money laundering law.

q.s: According to the EAC-PM working paper of September 2024, the five southern States together account for:
o: About 15 per cent of India's GDP
Over 30 per cent of India's GDP
Over 45 per cent of India's GDP
About 20 per cent of India's GDP
q.x: The southern States produce over 30% of GDP; in 2023-24 AP's share was 4.7% and Telangana's 4.9%.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Rythu Seva Kendras were earlier known as:
q.x: The village-level farmer service centres were renamed Rythu Seva Kendras.

q.s: The 'Stree Shakti' scheme of Andhra Pradesh provides:
o: Free bus travel for women in APSRTC buses
q.x: Stree Shakti free travel runs on APSRTC buses.

q.s: After bifurcation, the revenue lost by Andhra Pradesh with Hyderabad consisted mainly of:
o: Corporate taxes, stamp duties and commercial taxes
q.x: The Hyderabad region gave nearly half of undivided AP's revenue; residual AP kept its agricultural base.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts in the Budget Estimates for 2026-27 are about:
q.x: 2026-27 BE is Rs 2,34,190 crore, about 19% above 2024-25 RE of Rs 1,91,142 crore.

q.s: Under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 was an Expert Committee to study alternatives for the new capital of Andhra Pradesh provided?
q.x: Section 6 provided the Expert Committee (report within six months); Section 94(3) provides support for capital buildings; Section 90 is Polavaram.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase of the:
q.x: The VCIC is the first phase of the ECEC, assisted by the ADB and implemented by APIIC.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is being developed with the assistance of the:
q.x: The ADB is the lead partner; NDB funds AP roads in a 70:30 ratio.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the annual marine fishing ban period is:
q.x: The 61-day ban runs from 15 April to 14 June; relief is Rs 20,000 per family from 2024-25.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Fisheries University is located at:
q.x: It is at Narsapur, West Godavari district.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Integrated Call Centre for farmers (toll-free 155251) is located at:
q.x: The call centre is at Gannavaram; Rythu Bharosa Kendras were launched on 30 May 2020.

q.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Centre was to examine within six months the feasibility of:
o: A new major port at Machilipatnam
A bullet train from Amaravati to Hyderabad
q.x: The Schedule asked for a feasibility study of a VCIC on the lines of the DMIC within six months of the appointed day.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024-29 targets what share of all-India port cargo by 2047?
q.x: It aims at 300 MTPA capacity and 20% of India's cargo by 2047.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board is the nodal body for:
q.x: The AP Maritime Board governs non-major ports; Visakhapatnam is a major port under the Union.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 (2024-29) sets a production target of:
q.x: EMP 4.0 targets US$50 bn of electronics production; the Semiconductor & Display Fab Policy 4.0 covers Fab and OSAT units.

q.s: The knowledge partner for agribusiness incubation under RKVY-RAFTAAR is:
q.x: MANAGE is the knowledge partner; agri-startups get up to Rs 25 lakh at the seed stage.

q.s: Atal Tinkering Labs in schools are run under the Atal Innovation Mission of:
q.x: AIM is a NITI Aayog initiative; AIM 2.0 runs till March 2028.

q.s: The NIDHI programme for nurturing innovations and start-ups, including PRAYAS for prototypes, is run by the:
q.x: NIDHI is a DST programme; ASPIRE (2015) is of the Ministry of MSME and Udyam Abhilasha of SIDBI.

q.s: The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of:
q.x: The Martian atmosphere is about 95% CO2; Jupiter and Saturn are mostly hydrogen and helium.

q.s: The blue-green colour of Uranus and Neptune is due to the presence of which gas in their atmospheres?
q.x: Methane absorbs red light, giving the two ice giants their blue-green tint.

q.s: India's Deep Ocean Mission, under which seamounts in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal have been surveyed, is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
q.x: The Deep Ocean Mission is run by MoES; its surveys found about 25 seamounts.

q.s: The Arctic is warming about how many times faster than the global average?
q.x: Arctic amplification comes partly from melting ice exposing darker ocean that absorbs more heat.

q.s: Which type of clouds traps heat and has a net warming effect on the Earth's surface?
q.x: High, thin cirrus clouds trap outgoing heat; low thick clouds reflect sunlight and cool.

q.s: The most essential condition for the formation of a tropical cyclone is a sea-surface temperature above about:
q.x: Cyclones need warm seas over a large area; latent heat of condensation is their energy source.

q.s: Tropical cyclones almost never form right at the Equator because:
o: Sea temperatures are too low there
The Coriolis force is absent there
q.x: They form between about 5 and 30 degrees latitude, where the Coriolis force can set up rotation.

q.s: The San (Bushmen) are traditional inhabitants of the:
q.x: The San live in the Kalahari; the Tuareg are nomads of the Sahara and the Bedouin of Arabia.

q.s: The Maasai, traditionally cattle pastoralists, live mainly in:
q.x: The Maasai live in the East African savannas of Kenya and Tanzania; the Fulani are West African pastoralists.

q.s: Nathu La pass, reopened for India-China border trade in 2006, links Sikkim with:
q.x: Nathu La (about 4,310 m) connects Gangtok with the Chumbi Valley; China halted pilgrims through it in 2017.

q.s: In 2024, Port Blair, the capital of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, was renamed:
q.x: Port Blair became Sri Vijaya Puram in 2024; Havelock and Neil Islands were renamed Swaraj Dweep and Shaheed Dweep in 2018.

q.s: Saddle Peak, the highest point of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, is located in:
q.x: Saddle Peak (about 732 m) is in North Andaman.

q.s: Asia's first rubber dam in Andhra Pradesh is built on which river?
q.x: The rubber dam is on the Janjavathi, a tributary of the Nagavali, in Vizianagaram district.

q.s: Jonnagiri, India's first private-sector gold mine, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Jonnagiri gold project is in Kurnool district.

q.s: The Penna river meets the Bay of Bengal at Utukuru in which district?
q.x: The Penna enters the sea near Utukuru in Nellore district.

q.s: Konaseema, known for coconut and banana, is part of which river's delta?
q.x: Konaseema is the Godavari delta; Yanam also lies in it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about El Nino is correct?
o: It is a warm current that replaces the cold current off the coast of Peru.
It occurs every year in the Indian Ocean.
It generally strengthens the Indian monsoon.
It is a cold current that appears off the coast of Peru.
q.x: El Nino is a warm current appearing every 3-7 years; it usually weakens the Indian monsoon.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) is chaired by the:
q.x: Under the DM Act 2005, the State Authority is chaired by the CM; the State Executive Committee by the Chief Secretary.

q.s: The Chenab river is formed by the union of which two streams at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh?
q.x: Chandra and Bhaga join at Tandi; the Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus.

q.s: The Tawi river of Jammu is a tributary of the:
q.x: The Tawi joins the Chenab; the Ravi also joins the Chenab in Pakistan.

q.s: At Farakka, the Ganga splits; which of its arms enters Bangladesh as the Padma?
q.x: The left arm is the Bhagirathi-Hooghly; the main right arm flows into Bangladesh as the Padma.

q.s: Strictly by basin area lying within present-day Andhra Pradesh, the largest river basin is that of the:
q.x: Only about 4.5% of the Godavari basin lies in present AP since most of the undivided State's part went to Telangana in 2014.

q.s: Since 3 December 2023, security of the Nagarjuna Sagar dam has been handed over to the:
q.x: The CRPF guards Nagarjuna Sagar after a dispute between AP and Telangana.

q.s: Which of the following Krishna river projects is NOT under the control of Andhra Pradesh after 2014?
q.x: AP controls Srisailam, Pulichintala and the Prakasam Barrage; Telangana controls Jurala and Nagarjuna Sagar.

q.s: According to NCERT, alluvial soils of India are generally:
o: Rich in phosphorus but poor in potash
Rich in potash but poor in phosphorus
Poor in both potash and lime
q.x: Alluvial soils have adequate potash but little phosphorus; their sand content decreases from west to east.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, castor is mainly grown on which type of soil?
q.x: Castor is a red-soil crop of Rayalaseema; deltaic alluvium grows paddy and sugarcane.

q.s: Which sub-type of red soil covers the largest share (about 30 per cent) of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Red earths with loamy sub-soil cover about 30%; clay base 12%, red loamy 9%, chalka 8%.

q.s: Which is the smallest, by area, of the four main soil groups of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Laterite covers only about 1%; red soils dominate, and deltaic and coastal alluvium covers about 5-6%.

q.s: A storm surge associated with a cyclone is best described as:
o: An abnormal rise of sea level pushed by cyclone winds and low pressure
A sudden fall of sea level before a cyclone
A wave caused by an undersea earthquake
A tidal bore travelling up a river
q.x: A high tide raises the baseline and makes surge flooding worse; tsunamis are caused by earthquakes.

q.s: In India's disaster management framework, the nodal ministry for landslides is the Ministry of:
q.x: The Ministry of Mines (through the GSI) is nodal for landslides; Defence for avalanches.

q.s: The nodal ministry for urban floods in India is the Ministry of:
q.x: MoHUA handles urban floods; MoEFCC is nodal for industrial and chemical disasters.

q.s: The headquarters of the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is located at:
q.x: UNDRR is in Geneva; UNESCO-IOC is in Paris, ADRC in Kobe and the International Tsunami Information Centre in Honolulu.

q.s: The Kedarnath disaster of June 2013 was mainly caused by:
q.x: Kedarnath was a cloudburst and flash flood; Chamoli (2021) was a rock-ice glacier flood.

q.s: The Chamoli disaster of February 2021 in Uttarakhand was a:
q.x: A rock-ice avalanche from Ronti peak caused a flood in the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga.

q.s: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction covers the period:
q.x: Sendai succeeded the Hyogo Framework (2005-2015); IDNDR was the 1990s decade.

q.s: The Hyogo Framework for Action (2005-2015) was adopted at:
q.x: The Hyogo Framework was adopted at Kobe in 2005; the Yokohama Strategy was of 1994.

q.s: Under the MMDR Act, 1957, minor minerals are regulated by the:
q.x: Major minerals are regulated by the Centre and minor minerals by the States; mica and barytes were made minor minerals in 2015.

q.s: Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh is famous for which mineral?
q.x: Nellore is the mica belt; Mangampet (Kadapa) is known for barytes and Vizianagaram for manganese.

q.s: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor that reached criticality on 6 April 2026 is located at:
q.x: The 500 MWe PFBR is at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, the start of India's second-stage nuclear programme.

q.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025 repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the:
o: Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
q.x: SHANTI replaced both the 1962 Act and the CLNDA 2010.

q.s: The Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest hydropower project, is on the river:
q.x: Three Gorges (22,500 MW) is on the Yangtze; Itaipu on the Parana; Belo Monte on the Xingu.

q.s: The Itaipu hydropower project, shared by Brazil and Paraguay, is on the river:
q.x: Itaipu (14,000 MW) is on the Parana.

q.s: At present, the largest producer of lac in India is:
q.x: Jharkhand leads (Chhattisgarh next); older keys say Bihar because Jharkhand was part of Bihar till 2000.

q.s: Kolleru Lake of Andhra Pradesh has been shrinking and turning eutrophic mainly because of:
o: Encroachment of the lake bed for aquaculture ponds
q.x: Aquaculture encroachment of the lake bed between the Godavari and Krishna deltas is the main cause.

q.s: Koyali in Gujarat is known for:
q.x: Koyali has an IOC refinery; Muri - aluminium; Aonla - fertilisers; Sivakasi - fireworks and matches.

q.s: Sivakasi in Tamil Nadu, called 'Little Japan', is famous for:
q.x: Sivakasi (Virudhunagar) is known for fireworks, matches and printing.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh node of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor is:
q.x: Krishnapatnam is the CBIC node; Orvakal (Kurnool) is the node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

q.s: The Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor is being developed along the:
q.x: AKIC is built on the Eastern DFC.

q.s: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur was set up in 1955 with the collaboration of:
q.x: ICF Perambur was built with Swiss collaboration; Chittaranjan Locomotive Works makes electric locomotives.

q.s: Under the One District One Product (ODOP) scheme, Budithi brassware represents which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Budithi brass is from Srikakulam; Narsapur crochet laces represent West Godavari.

q.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the highest number of Udyam-registered MSMEs?
q.x: Anantapur has about 2.37 lakh Udyam-registered MSMEs.

q.s: India's first cable-stayed rail bridge, on the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link, is the:
q.x: Anji Khad is the first cable-stayed rail bridge; Chenab is the world's highest railway arch bridge.

q.s: The Atal Tunnel (9.02 km), the world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet, lies under the:
q.x: Atal Tunnel runs under the Rohtang Pass, linking Manali with Lahaul-Spiti.

q.s: The longest National Waterway of India is:
q.x: NW-1 from Haldia to Prayagraj is the longest; NW-2 runs from Sadiya to Dhubri.

q.s: Jogighopa and Tezpur are terminals on National Waterway 2, which lies on the river:
q.x: NW-2 is on the Brahmaputra; the CIWTC is headquartered at Kolkata.

q.s: Lepakshi, known for its hanging pillar and the largest monolithic Nandi, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Lepakshi and Penukonda fort are in Sri Sathya Sai district.

q.s: Kondapalli Fort, also famous for wooden toys, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Kondapalli is in NTR district after the 2022 district reorganisation.

q.s: Under the ULLAS (Nav Bharat Saksharta Karyakram) scheme, 'full literacy' means literacy of at least:
o: 95 per cent among persons aged 15 and above
90 per cent among persons aged 7 and above
q.x: A State is declared fully literate at 95% literacy among those aged 15+.

q.s: The Quality of Life for Elderly Index (August 2021) was released by the:
o: Economic Advisory Council to the PM
q.x: Bibek Debroy of the EAC-PM released it; Rajasthan led the aged States and Chandigarh the UTs.

q.s: As per Census 2011, India's rural and urban sex ratios were respectively:
q.x: Rural 949, urban 929 (overall 943); undivided AP's rural and urban figures were 996 and 987.

q.s: According to the Census, a 'main worker' is one who worked for at least how many days in the reference year?
q.x: Main workers worked 183 days (six months) or more; marginal workers less than that.

q.s: As per NFHS-5, the total sex ratio (females per 1,000 males) of Andhra Pradesh was about:
q.x: NFHS-5 total sex ratio was about 1,045 (India 1,020); AP's sex ratio at birth was 934 and Census 2011 figure 997.

q.s: Pilani in Rajasthan is an example of which functional type of town?
q.x: Pilani, Roorkee and Aligarh are educational towns; Kandla is a port, Araku a resort and Bhadrachalam a religious town.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a push factor of migration?
q.x: Education at the destination is a pull factor; the others push people out of the origin.

q.s: The Lokur Committee (1965) is known for laying down the:
q.x: Lokur gave the ST criteria; Dhebar created the PTG category; the Bhuria Committee led to PESA.

q.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee (1994-95) recommended self-rule in Scheduled Areas.

q.s: According to the Constitution of India, Hindi in Devanagari script is:
o: The only language of the Supreme Court
The official language of the Union
The official language of all States
q.x: Article 343 makes Hindi the Union's official language; the Constitution names no national language.

q.s: Which law allowed English to continue alongside Hindi for official purposes after 1965?
q.x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 provided for English to continue after the 15-year transition.

q.s: The geoengineering proposal of 'marine cloud brightening' involves spraying which substance into marine clouds?
q.x: Sea-salt particles act as condensation nuclei; stratospheric sulphate injection is a different proposal with a 'termination shock' risk.

q.s: Countries such as Japan and Germany, where the birth rate has fallen below the death rate, are in which stage of demographic transition?
q.x: Declining (stage 5) - Japan, Germany; low stationary - Andhra Pradesh; late expanding - Brazil; early expanding - Niger.

q.s: The IndiaAI Mission approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2024 has an outlay of about:
q.x: The mission (MeitY) has an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore and plans over 10,000 GPUs of compute.

q.s: Under the IndiaAI Mission, 'AI-Kosh' is a:
q.x: AI-Kosh is the IndiaAI Datasets Platform; foundation models come under the Innovation Centre pillar.

q.s: 'AP DigiVerify' of the Andhra Pradesh government uses which technology to verify certificates?
q.x: AP DigiVerify is a permissioned-blockchain platform for certificate verification.

q.s: Which Indian private company set up the 'Dhanush' private launch pad at Sriharikota?
q.x: Agnikul (Agnibaan rocket) built Dhanush; Skyroot builds Vikram rockets.

q.s: 'Firefly', the first Indian private commercial satellite constellation (January 2025), consists of:
q.x: Pixxel's Firefly satellites are hyperspectral imagers; GalaxEye's Drishti combines SAR and optical.

q.s: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change, released in 2008, comprises how many national missions?
q.x: The NAPCC has eight missions, including the National Solar Mission and Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency.

q.s: The nodal unit for India's negotiations under the UNFCCC is the:
o: Prime Minister's Council on Climate Change
q.x: MoEFCC's Climate Change Division handles UNFCCC negotiations; the PM's Council sets policy.

q.s: Which of the following is an in-situ bioremediation technique?
q.x: Biosparging treats contamination in place; landfarming, composting and biopiles are ex-situ, with bioreactors the fastest.

q.s: 'Phytorid', a constructed-wetland technology for treating sewage, was developed by:
q.x: Phytorid is NEERI's; TERI with Indian Oil developed Oilzapper for oil spills.

q.s: The fullerene molecule C60 is commonly known as:
q.x: C60 is the buckyball (Nobel 1996); graphene is a one-atom-thick sheet (Nobel 2010).

q.s: Which metal is popularly called the 'metal of the future'?
q.x: Titanium is so called for its strength, lightness and corrosion resistance.

q.s: The Department of Space in India functions directly under the:
q.x: DoS reports to the PM; the ISRO Chairman is also Secretary, DoS and Chairman of the Space Commission.

q.s: Dr V. Narayanan, who became Chairman of ISRO in January 2025, succeeded:
q.x: V. Narayanan is the 11th Chairman of ISRO, after S. Somanath.

q.s: A geostationary satellite orbits the Earth above the equator at a height of about:
q.x: GEO height (period 24 hours) is fixed and does not depend on the satellite's mass.

q.s: Which of the following is India's satellite-based augmentation system (SBAS)?
q.x: GAGAN is India's SBAS; WAAS - USA, EGNOS - Europe, MSAS - Japan.

q.s: The Crew Module Atmospheric Re-entry Experiment (CARE) of 2014 was launched on the:
q.x: CARE flew on the first experimental LVM3 in 2014; SRE-1 flew on PSLV-C7 in 2007.

q.s: RISAT-1, launched by PSLV-C19 in 2012, carries which type of radar?
q.x: RISAT-1 carries a C-band SAR.

q.s: EOS-08, launched in August 2024, flew on the last development flight of which launch vehicle?
q.x: SSLV-D3 carried EOS-08; SSLV-D2 had carried EOS-07 in February 2023.

q.s: Nirbhay, developed by DRDO, is a:
q.x: Nirbhay is turbojet powered, flies at about Mach 0.8 and has a range of about 1,000 km.

q.s: The 'Manik' small turbofan engine for the Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile was developed by:
q.x: The Gas Turbine Research Establishment of DRDO developed Manik.

q.s: India's first nuclear test, Pokhran-I (1974), was a:
q.x: Pokhran-I ('Smiling Buddha') was a fission device using plutonium.

q.s: The Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system developed by DRDO's NMRL is based on:
q.x: The indigenous fuel-cell AIP lets diesel-electric submarines stay submerged longer.

q.s: The 'Uttam' AESA radar for the Tejas Mk-1A was developed by:
q.x: LRDE, Bengaluru developed Uttam; an AESA radar steers its beam electronically.

q.s: Over-the-horizon radars detect distant targets by bouncing which waves off the ionosphere?
q.x: OTH radars use HF waves reflected by the ionosphere.

q.s: Cordite, a smokeless propellant, contains:
q.x: Cordite is nitroglycerine plus nitrocellulose; amatol is TNT plus ammonium nitrate.

q.s: Gun cotton is chemically:
q.x: Gun cotton is made by treating cotton with nitric and sulphuric acids.

q.s: 'Punarvas', an NIC Andhra Pradesh solution that won a National e-Governance Award in 2018, handles compensation for families displaced by the:
q.x: Punarvas handles compensation for Kovvada displaced families; Jeevandan is the cadaver-organ portal.

q.s: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, set up in 1983 by an executive order, got statutory status under the:
q.x: AERB became statutory under the SHANTI Act, 2025; the NSRA Bill was never enacted.

q.s: India's Ethanol Blended Petrol programme began in January 2003 with what level of blending?
q.x: EBP began with 5% blending; India reached 20% (E20) in 2025.

q.s: The large low-grade uranium deposit at Tummalapalle is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Tummalapalle in YSR Kadapa district is among the world's largest uranium deposits.

q.s: Among the world's coal producers, India ranks:
q.x: India is second after China and has the fifth-largest coal reserves.

q.s: India's key supplier of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) is:
q.x: Qatar is the main LNG supplier; India is the third-largest oil consumer.

q.s: India's rank among the world's oil-consuming countries is:
q.x: India is the third-largest oil consumer after the USA and China.

q.s: The RUCO initiative for converting used cooking oil into biodiesel was launched by:
q.x: RUCO (Repurpose Used Cooking Oil) is an FSSAI initiative.

q.s: Under the Bharat Stage VI norms, the maximum sulphur content allowed in diesel is:
q.x: BS-II 500, BS-III 350, BS-IV 50 and BS-VI 10 ppm.

q.s: Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) used in BS-VI diesel vehicles converts NOx into nitrogen and water using:
q.x: SCR uses urea (AdBlue); a Diesel Particulate Filter traps soot.

q.s: The Makum coalfield is located in which State?
q.x: Makum - Assam; Talcher - Odisha; Korba - Chhattisgarh; Mawlong - Meghalaya.

q.s: India became the world's third-largest solar power producer by overtaking:
q.x: India overtook Japan; China is the largest.

q.s: In installed wind power capacity, India ranks:
q.x: India is 4th in wind and 3rd in total renewable capacity.

q.s: In India, small hydro projects up to what capacity come under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy?
q.x: MNRE handles small hydro up to 25 MW (ceiling raised from 3 MW in 1999); large hydro is with the Ministry of Power.

q.s: Large hydropower projects were declared part of renewable energy in:
q.x: Large hydro (above 25 MW) was classed as renewable in March 2019.

q.s: The largest pumped storage project of Andhra Pradesh is the:
q.x: Upper Sileru (1,350 MW) is the largest; AP's 2022 policy identified 29 sites of 33,240 MW.

q.s: The State nodal agency for solar energy development in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: NEDCAP (New and Renewable Energy Development Corporation of AP) is the nodal agency.

q.s: Which country was the first to cross 1 terawatt (TW) of installed solar capacity?
q.x: China is the largest solar producer and first past 1 TW; India added about 38 GW in 2025.

q.s: India's installed pumped storage hydro capacity is only about:
q.x: Of a potential of about 267 GW, only about 7 GW is installed; AP's potential is about 42,020 MW.

q.s: The 1,000 MW ultra mega solar park, once the world's largest single-location solar park, is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park (Panyam) was once the world's largest; Galiveedu (Kadapa) is also 1,000 MW.

q.s: Energy flow in an ecosystem is:
q.x: Energy flows one way from producers to consumers; nutrients are cycled.

q.s: Species diversity of an area takes into account:
q.x: Species diversity considers richness (number) and evenness (relative abundance).

q.s: Biodiversity hotspots, which once covered about 15.7% of the Earth's land, now cover only about:
q.x: They still hold about 50% of vascular plants and 42% of terrestrial vertebrates as endemics.

q.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
q.x: It was launched at Suratgarh; a card is issued every 2 years.

q.s: Under the Soil Health Card scheme, a card is issued to farmers once every:
q.x: Cards are issued every two years with crop-wise nutrient recommendations.

q.s: Coal-based thermal power plants in India are required to co-fire what share of biomass in FY 2025-26?
q.x: Co-firing rose from 5% in FY 2024-25 to 7%, monitored by the SAMARTH mission.

q.s: CITES, the convention on trade in endangered species, was signed in 1973 at:
q.x: CITES was signed at Washington on 3 March 1973; its secretariat is at Geneva under UNEP.

q.s: Project Elephant was launched by the Government of India in:
q.x: Project Elephant (1992) covers habitats, corridors, conflict and welfare of captive elephants; Project Tiger began in 1973.

q.s: Which of the following litter items takes the longest time to degrade?
q.x: Paper takes weeks, wool about a year, metal cans 100-500 years and plastic bags far longer.

q.s: The SATAT initiative of the Government of India promotes:
q.x: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) promotes CBG plants; FAME-II gave EV subsidies.

q.s: The pH of normal (unpolluted) rain water is about:
q.x: Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, giving normal rain a pH of about 5.6; acid rain is below that.

q.s: The term 'acid rain' was coined in 1852 by:
q.x: Robert Angus Smith coined it while studying Manchester's air.

q.s: Blackfoot disease is caused by the presence of which element in drinking water?
q.x: Arsenic causes blackfoot disease; cadmium causes itai-itai and mercury Minamata disease.

q.s: The 1991 notification declaring Dahanu Taluka ecologically fragile and barring power plants there relates to which State?
q.x: Dahanu (Palghar district) is in Maharashtra; the Doon Valley notification of 1989 relates to Uttarakhand.

q.s: The Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative (SSI) uses which planting material?
q.x: SSI uses single-bud chips raised in nurseries, saving seed cane and water.

q.s: Wet-bulb temperature becomes equal to dry-bulb temperature when relative humidity is:
q.x: In saturated air no water evaporates from the wet bulb, so there is no evaporative cooling.

q.s: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is spread by the:
q.x: The tsetse fly spreads sleeping sickness; the sandfly spreads kala-azar.

q.s: Kyasanur Forest Disease ('monkey fever') spreads to humans through:
q.x: KFD of Shivamogga, Karnataka is a tick-borne viral disease.

q.s: Under the 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, the fine for violence against health workers ranges from:
q.x: The offence is cognizable and non-bailable; grievous hurt draws higher fines and 6 months to 7 years.

q.s: INSACOG, set up in December 2020, is a:
q.x: INSACOG is a consortium of labs (DBT, ICMR, CSIR, MoHFW) for variant sequencing; U-WIN tracks immunisation.

q.s: The DPT vaccine protects against:
q.x: DPT covers diphtheria, pertussis (whooping cough) and tetanus; BCG against TB is given at birth.

q.s: Tetanus is caused by the bacterium:
q.x: Clostridium tetani causes tetanus; smallpox was caused by the variola virus.

q.s: The National Innovation Foundation-India, an autonomous body of DST set up in March 2000, is located at:
q.x: NIF-India is at Gandhinagar; its Festival of Innovation is held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

q.s: The National Innovation Foundation grew out of the 'Honey Bee Network' founded by:
o: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
q.x: Prof. Anil K. Gupta's Honey Bee Network documented grassroots innovations.

q.s: The India International Science Festival (IISF) is organised by the Ministries of Science and Technology and Earth Sciences together with:
q.x: IISF, begun in 2015, is held with Vijnana Bharati; its 11th edition was at Panchkula in December 2025.

q.s: The Indian Science Congress Association, founded in 1914, is headquartered at:
q.x: ISCA is at Kolkata; its first session (1914) was presided over by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee.

q.s: The Online Gaming Authority of India under the Online Gaming Act, 2025 is an attached office of the:
o: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
q.x: The Authority is under MeitY; the Act bans real-money gaming.

q.s: Gig workers and platform workers were first defined in law in the:
q.x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 first defined gig and platform workers.

q.s: In 2025, SEBI proposed allowing Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to trade in:
q.x: The proposal (gold, silver, base metals) aims at far-month liquidity, price discovery and hedging.

q.s: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), linked to the BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week, was launched by India at:
q.x: PM Modi announced LiFE at COP26 (2021); the week was observed under India's BRICS Presidency.

q.s: Non-permanent members of the UN Security Council are elected for a term of:
q.x: The UNGA elects them by a two-thirds majority; they cannot be re-elected immediately.

q.s: The UN World Food Programme, with which India signed a rice supply agreement, is headquartered at:
q.x: WFP (1961) is in Rome and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020.

q.s: The World Food Programme was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in:
q.x: WFP won the 2020 Nobel Peace Prize for combating hunger.

q.s: India's Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) has been signed with:
q.x: TEPA - EFTA (USD 100 bn FDI commitment); CETA - UK; ECTA - Australia; CECPA - Mauritius.

q.s: India's first trade agreement with an African country, the CECPA (2021), was signed with:
q.x: The Comprehensive Economic Cooperation and Partnership Agreement with Mauritius was India's first with an African nation.

q.s: Which country was the first to recognise the rights of nature ('Pacha Mama') in its national constitution, in 2008?
q.x: Articles 71-74 of Ecuador's 2008 Constitution give rights to nature.

q.s: Under the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, which sector did India keep protected from tariff liberalisation?
q.x: India protected dairy, cereals, poultry and soymeal; the EU liberalised 97% and India 92.1% of tariff lines.

q.s: In August 2025, the WHO declared that Nepal had eliminated which disease as a public health problem?
q.x: Nepal was declared free of rubella, which can cause Congenital Rubella Syndrome in infants.

q.s: The Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) scheme was created by:
q.x: Sections 7A-7D of the 2003 Amendment created OCI; the PIO card merged into OCI in 2015.

q.s: The PIO Card scheme was merged with the OCI scheme in:
q.x: PIO cards were merged into OCI in 2015; India still does not permit dual citizenship.

q.s: The first international campus of an IIT, IIT Madras Zanzibar, is located in:
